Todd County sits in southwestern Kentucky with Elkton as the county seat. It is a small rural county with a strong farm base and a long local history. For tax sale investors, Todd County is a Kentucky tax lien county, not a tax deed county. That means buyers purchase a lien called a certificate of delinquency, not the property itself. This guide explains how Todd County tax sales work, where updates are posted, what the registration rules are, and what investors should check before they spend money.

What is Todd County’s tax sale system?

Todd County follows Kentucky’s certificate of delinquency system. When real property taxes stay unpaid and move from the sheriff to the county clerk, they become certificates of delinquency. Those certificates can then be sold to third party purchasers at the county tax sale. In simple terms, you are buying the tax lien. You are not buying the house or land on sale day. The lien earns interest and may later be enforced through foreclosure if it stays unpaid long enough.

Important Details

Key Takeaways

  • Todd County, located in southwestern Kentucky, operates on a tax lien certificate system, allowing buyers to purchase liens rather than properties.
  • Tax sales in Todd County occur between mid-July and late August, requiring registration with the county clerk.
  • Investors earn 1 percent simple interest per month on certificates, which can lead to significant returns if unpaid.
  • Due diligence is crucial when investing in Todd County tax liens; researchers should verify property details and conditions before bidding.
  • Todd County offers a manageable investment environment, making it suitable for both local and out-of-state investors.

Fun Facts About the County

  • Todd County’s population estimate was 12,972 in 2025.
  • The county was formed in 1820 and Elkton is the county seat.
  • Todd County led Kentucky in organic agriculture in 2022 with 16 farms marketing more than $7.1 million in organic products.
  • The county is tied to Robert Penn Warren and John Todd in Kentucky history.

Attractions & Economic Highlights

  • Historic Todd County runs a welcome center on Public Square in Elkton.
  • U.S. 79 runs through Todd County and the county is part of Kentucky Highway District 3.
  • Agriculture stays important here and organic farming has been a strong local story.
  • Small business, farming, and local heritage help shape county life.

Why This County is Ideal for Tax Lien Investors

  • Kentucky tax lien certificates can offer high returns through 1 percent monthly simple interest.
  • Todd County is a smaller market, which may feel easier to review than a large urban list. This is an investor view based on county size and sale format.
  • State tax lien opportunities here follow a clear Kentucky system with published rules.
  • Agriculture and rural land can create niche value for buyers who know how to review acreage, access, and use.

Auction Process for Todd County, Kentucky tax lien sales

Todd County uses Kentucky’s lien sale process rather than a bid down interest auction. The interest rate is set by law at 1 percent per month. Buyers do not compete by lowering that rate. Instead, registered buyers submit their lists, attend the sale, and then certificates are assigned through a random drawing and round based selection process. That is an important point for anyone used to Florida or other bid down states.

How the Auction Works

  1. Register before the deadline

    File the county clerk form and any required state registration proof if your purchase level triggers state filing.

  2. Submit your purchase lists

    You must give the clerk your priority list and your current year list before the deadline.

  3. Bring the right deposit

    Priority claims need a 100 percent deposit. Current year lists need a 25 percent deposit.

  4. Attend the drawing

    Selection order is set by random drawing at the start of the sale.

  5. Select in rounds

    Certificates are sold in rounds and lot sizes depend on how many liens are in the sale.

  6. Pay the balance

    Your deposit is applied first. Any extra amount due must be paid as the clerk requires.

A note on Todd County itself. The most recent official postings do not fully match. Kentucky’s state sale date list showed Todd County on August 14, 2025, while the Todd County Clerk delinquent tax page showed a sale at 9 AM on September 14, 2025. Because of that conflict, investors should check the live county notice before they travel or wire funds.

Maximum Potential Returns and Expected Returns on Todd County tax lien certificates

The base return in Kentucky is simple interest of 1 percent per month on the certificate balance. That works out to 12 percent per year if the lien stays unpaid for a full year. There can also be allowed fees tied to the lien process, but those must follow Kentucky rules. The return depends on how fast the owner pays, whether notices are handled the right way, and whether you ever need to move into foreclosure. A fast payoff can still be a good yield. A slow file can tie up cash for much longer.

Open to All Investors and foreign investor participation

Kentucky allows third party purchasers to register as individuals or entities. The state materials talk about entity type, contact details, tax compliance, and ownership information. They do not limit the process to local residents on the pages reviewed here. That means out of county and out of state investors can take part if they meet the rules. Foreign investors should also be able to participate through a proper legal structure, but they should get tax and legal advice first, especially if farm land or later foreclosure is involved.

Importance of Due Diligence in Todd County tax lien investing

Buying a Todd County tax lien is not the same as buying a clean deed. You are buying a lien claim that may later need collection work, notices, or foreclosure.

What Due Diligence Entails

  • Check the PVA record and parcel details before the sale.
  • Review access, road frontage, and actual land use.
  • Check if the parcel is occupied, vacant, farm land, or has a structure.
  • Estimate whether the lien size matches the work and time involved.
  • Read Kentucky notice, fee, and foreclosure rules before bidding.

Risks of Skipping Due Diligence

  • You may buy a hard to collect lien.
  • You may face extra time and legal cost.
  • You may end up with land that is hard to resell after foreclosure.
  • Bad address research can slow notices and suspend fee or interest accrual.

Buying Over the Counter liens in Todd County

How to Purchase OTC liens

Yes. Kentucky allows unsold certificates to be bought after the auction. The state guide says any remaining certificates of delinquency may be purchased at any time by any third party purchaser after the sale, as long as the buyer still meets the registration rules. Start with the Todd County Clerk and ask for the current unsold list and payment instructions.

Benefits of OTC Purchases

OTC buying can be easier because there is no sale day rush. You can review the file more calmly. The tradeoff is that the best liens may already be gone.

Why Todd County is a top choice for tax lien investors

Economic and Tax Advantages

  • Kentucky gives a clear lien system with published forms and rules.
  • Todd County has a farm based economy with real land use value.
  • The county’s small size can make list review more manageable.

Real Estate Market Overview

Todd County is rural. That usually means lower pricing than large metro counties, but it also means buyers must study access, utilities, and resale demand more closely. For investors who know land and small town property, that can be useful. For beginners, it means slow down and verify every parcel before you bid.

Conclusion

Todd County, Kentucky is a tax lien certificate market. It is not a tax deed market on sale day. Buyers get a lien that earns 1 percent simple interest per month and may later be enforced if unpaid. The county clerk is the main local source for sale notices, registration deadlines, and contact details, while the Kentucky Department of Revenue explains the wider rules on timing, deposits, fees, and post sale collection. Todd County can make sense for investors who like smaller county lists and rural property research. Just make sure you confirm the live sale notice because recent official postings showed a date mismatch. Good research is what turns a tax lien from a gamble into a smart investing move.

Pro Tips

  • Focus first on parcels with simple ownership and clear map data.
  • In Todd County, pay close attention to farm access and road frontage.
  • Call the clerk before sale week if the county page and state list do not match.
  • Keep cash free for post sale OTC buys that other bidders pass on.
  • Treat every lien like a collection file first and a property play second.

Todd County tax lien FAQs

Do I own the property right after the sale?

No. You buy the tax lien, not the deed.

Can I start foreclosure right away?

No. Kentucky bars enforcement action for at least one year.

Can the owner ask for payments over time?

Yes. A written request can trigger an installment plan.

Will I need title cleanup later?

Often yes if a lien goes through foreclosure and you plan to resell.

Can I finance my bids?

County and state materials focus on deposits and payment, so plan on ready funds.
